Hi Maya — great to hear. Summary below plus a lightweight activation checklist attached. Let me know if you'd prefer a shared doc for live edits.

High-level answers:
- Org & API keys: We can either (A) provision a Redwood org for NovaBio and invite your SSO admin (preferred for fastest onboarding), or (B) you can create the org and add our service account. Our team typically provisions the initial API keys and hands them over via DocuSign; we recommend rotating keys after the POC.
- IP allowlist: Redwood hosted egress runs from a small set of static CIDR blocks per region. I attached ip-allowlist-novabio.csv with the US egress ranges you can add to your firewall.
- VPC peering: We support VPC peering with a standard template — see vpc-peering-template.txt attached. We prefer non-overlapping /22 CIDRs but can accept /20 for larger workloads; we’ll provide the peer IP and security group rules during the peering window.

Proposed MAP / POC activation timeline (week-by-week):
1) Week 0 (this week): MAP sign-off — agree scope, timeline, and success criteria.
2) Week 1: Org provisioning + initial API key handover (DocuSign).
3) Week 2: IP allowlist added by NovaBio; connectivity smoke test.
4) Week 3: VPC peering scheduled and validated; token rotation policy configured.
5) Week 4: Load-weighted run and performance check; go/no-go for expansion.

Action items for NovaBio this week:
- Confirm preferred org model (Redwood-provisioned vs NovaBio-provisioned).
- Share service account email(s) for peering and API integrations.
- Apply ip-allowlist-novabio.csv to firewall when ready and confirm test IP.

Attaching: MAP_NovaBio_v1.2.pdf (MAP draft), vpc-peering-template.txt, ip-allowlist-novabio.csv.

If this looks good I’ll send a DocuSign for the MAP sign-off and slot the Week 2 peering window on 12/15-12/16 as a placeholder.

Thanks — Sean

Aaron / Maya — quick technical notes from infra that will help your networking team: 

1) Peering CIDR guidance: for the POC we recommend allocating a /24 (e.g., 10.240.32.0/24) specifically for the peering interface to simplify route tables. Production peering can be /20 or /19 depending on scale, but please avoid overlapping internal ranges.
2) Service account & IAM: please provide a dedicated service account email we can add to the org for auditing. That account will receive API key provisioning notifications and be listed in the MAP.
3) Firewall rules: allow outbound/tcp to our egress IPs on ports 443 and 5222 (we use 5222 for internal health check traffic in some regions).
4) Token rotation: we recommend cadence of 90 days for POC; let us know if your security policy requires shorter cycles.
